subject: bristlecone pine
title: What If Someone Cut Down the Oldest Tree on Earth? In 1964 It Happened

scenes.text: What if someone cut down the oldest tree on Earth? In 1964, someone did. With permission.
Summer 1964, Wheeler Peak, Nevada. A graduate student is reading ancient climate in the rings of bristlecone pines.
One tree won't give him a clean sample. By some accounts, his coring tool breaks. The Forest Service lets him cut it down.
Only afterwards does he count the rings. Four thousand, eight hundred and sixty-two.
The tree, known as Prometheus, was around 4,900 years old, the oldest tree anyone had ever dated.
Bristlecones are now protected on federal land, and the grove became part of a national park in 1986. Only the stump remains.

description:
What if the oldest known tree on Earth were cut down? In August 1964 a graduate student studying past climate cut down a Great Basin bristlecone pine on Wheeler Peak, Nevada, with the permission of the US Forest Service. Accounts differ on why: a broken or stuck coring tool, or the need for a full cross-section.
The tree, called Prometheus, had 4,862 countable rings and was about 4,900 years old, the oldest tree then known. Its grove became part of Great Basin National Park in 1986, and bristlecone pines are now protected on federal land.
